original_interpretation: EUV (NXE+EXE) made up about 47% of ASML's 2025 net system sales (EUR 11.6bn of EUR 24.5bn) and ArF immersion about 42%; KrF, ArF dry and i-line together were under 7%.
evidence_found: Note on disaggregation of revenue, p. 280: "Net system sales per technology were as follows: Year ended December 31 2023 2024 2025 in units in € millions ... ... Metrology & Inspection 151 536.1 165 645.5 208 824.6 Total 600 21,938.6 583 21,768.7 535 24,474.3"
notes: Re-opened the ASML 2025 Annual Report PDF at the cited URL (full PDF retrieved via browser and text-extracted; 354 pages). Recomputed: (1,156.9+10,445.8)/24,474.3 = 47.4%; 10,311.4/24,474.3 = 42.1%; (427.0+1,001.3+307.3)/24,474.3 = 7.09%. Denominator includes EUR 824.6m metrology & inspection (3.4%). The record's own evidence line computes 7.1%, contradicting the 'under 7%' wording.
correction: KrF + ArF dry + i-line = EUR 1,735.6m = 7.09% of EUR 24,474.3m net system sales, i.e. slightly ABOVE 7%, not 'under 7%'. EUV 47.4% and ArF immersion 42.1% are correct. See superseding inference claim.

original_interpretation: In November 2025 the EU incorporated certain Dutch national controls into the EU Control List, extending a licence requirement for advanced equipment such as DUV immersion lithography systems to all EU member states; ASML says this changed nothing for it because those products already needed a Dutch licence.

For ASML this did not mean a change as these products already required an export license from the Netherlands."

FCF-floor prepayments are conditional ('if certain criteria are met'), consistent with the claim's 'may'.

original_interpretation: Since the May 2025 restatement, ASML's capex loans to Carl Zeiss SMT are interest-free with 7- or 15-year expected terms; in 2025 ASML lent EUR 444 million long-term plus short-term loans of EUR 169 million and EUR 212.5 million.
evidence_found: Note 26, p. 320: "Loans are interest-free with an expected repayment term of either 7 or 15 years" ... "In July 2025 we provided a loan to Carl Zeiss SMT GmbH for an amount of €444 million." ... "In June 2025 we provided a short-term loan ... €169 million. This loan was fully repaid in November 2025." ... "In November 2025 ... another short-term loan ... €212.5 million."
notes: Re-opened the ASML 2025 Annual Report PDF at the cited URL (full PDF retrieved via browser and text-extracted; 354 pages). Interest-free 7/15-year terms apply to capex loans 'as from 2025'; the earlier 2021 and 2024 loan agreements carry interest (floor 0.01%, cap 1%; 2024 loan EIR 3.1%).
correction: All figures correct, but the report does not label the EUR 444m loan as 'long-term' or explicitly as a capex loan (it is listed under '2025 loan agreements', EIR 3.3%, amortized cost EUR 333.2m). The short-term loans fall under a separate supply-chain support commitment (interest-free, 1-year term), not the capex facility; the EUR 169m loan was fully repaid in November 2025.
